question: When is Kali Pooja celebrated in West Bengal region?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kartika Amavasya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kartika Amavasya:**

 
 
• This significant day falls during the Hindu month of Kartik (typically October/November).
 
• It is observed for ancestral rites, particularly to appease departed ancestors. Rituals like 'shraddha' (ancestral offerings), 'tarpan' (water libations), and 'pind daan' (food offerings) are performed to honor and seek blessings from ancestors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kartika Poornima:**

 
 
• This day marks the culmination of the Kartik month and is celebrated as Diwali, the Festival of Lights. Diwali symbolizes the victory of good over evil and the triumph of light over darkness.
 
• Homes are illuminated with diyas (earthen lamps), and festivities include fireworks, prayers to Lakshmi (goddess of wealth), and the exchange of sweets.
 
 
 
• **Ashwin Amavasya:**
 
 
• **​** Also known as Mahalaya Amavasya or Pitru Amavasya, this day in the Ashwin month (September/October) is dedicated to ancestral rites.
 
• It is believed that ancestors visit the Earth on this day, and rituals are performed to offer them respect and ensure their peaceful journey.
 
 
 
• **Ashwin Poornima:**
 
 
• This full moon day in Ashwin is known as Kojagiri Purnima in some regions.
 
• It is a time for prayers to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth. Women often observe fasts and perform special rituals to seek blessings for prosperity and well-being.
